title: SRE weekly ops sync notes - 2026-03-15 (draft)
content:
Meeting: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review (prep notes)
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 09:30-10:15 PT
Attendees (prelim): Jordan Lee (owner), Priya Nair, Samir Patel, Maya Gomez, Taro Ishikawa (oncall), optional: Product infra reps
Goals for this sync:
- Quick SLO snapshot + error budget burn updates
- Paging trends + root-cause patterns week-over-week
- Review top incidents since last sync, verify postmortem status and action ownership
- Decide on runbook updates + scheduling oncall run-throughs

Prep metrics (snapshot as of 2026-03-14 23:59 UTC)
- Global availability SLO (service-facing): target 99.95% monthly
  - Current month: 99.91% -> 0.04% below target -> ~35% of monthly error budget burned (projected full-month burn: ~1.2x if current rate continues)
- Inference API p99 latency SLO: target 400ms
  - Current week median p99: 420ms (spike during 2026-03-10 incident)
- Paging count (last 7 days): 18 pages (vs 27 previous week)
  - Pages by team: inference-runtime (8), router (4), kv-cache (3), other infra (3)
- Top alert flapping alerts: GPU-mem-high (infra), router-504-rate

Paging trends + quick analysis:
- Overall paging volume down ~30% vs prior week. Good signal — possibly due to the auto-scaling fixes rolled 3/9. Need to confirm correlation with deployment windows (ask infra).
- inference-runtime pages are concentrated around memory pressure / OOMs and large-batch requests. Revisit batching config recommendations from Optimize to avoid pathological memory growth.
- router 504s: correlated with increased tail latency on dedicated hosts in us-west-2 during peak traffic window (11:00–12:30 PT). Likely partial network blips + fallback path not warm.

Top incidents since last sync (brief)
1) SRE-INC-2134 (2026-03-10) — inference-runtime OOM cascade -> 12 minutes elevated errors
   - Symptom: 10% error rate for inference requests across dedicated pools (us-west-2) for ~12m.
   - Root cause (postmortem draft): KV cache eviction failure + large concurrent batched requests caused memory growth beyond anticipated working set.
   - Immediate mitigations: throttled large-batch API, increased eviction aggressiveness (hotfix), restart of 3 affected nodes.
   - Action items: infra to add memory-watermark alert + automated eviction trigger (owner: Priya, due 2026-03-22). Update runbook for OOM handling (owner: Jordan, due 2026-03-18).
   - Status: postmortem draft in Jira (SRE-INC-2134), review scheduled for 3/16.

2) INFRA-4521 (2026-03-12) — router partial degradation -> intermittent 504s
   - Symptom: ~1% request 504s for 40 minutes during peak; router fallback to slower tier increased p99.
   - Root cause: network flaps to a subset of dedicated hosts + gap in fallback routing warm-up.
   - Actions: implement pre-warm of fallback pools during scale events (owner: Samir, due 2026-03-29). Add extra instrumentation (owner: Maya, due 2026-03-20).
   - Status: incident closed; engineering PR open for fallback warm-up (link in linked_artifacts).

Runbook / process items to discuss
- OOM handling: add explicit memory-watermark alert, automated KV eviction, and clear escalation steps. Current runbook lacks actionable memory thresholds.
- Paging thresholds: consider raising low-priority pager cadence for router-504 from P1 to P2 if we have automated mitigations in place. Need SRE consensus.
- Oncall fatigue: fewer pages this week but several high-severity bursts. Propose experiment: allow oncall to opt into async follow-ups for non-customer affecting incidents (pilot 2 weeks).

Agenda (meeting)
1) Quick SLO snapshot (5m) — Jordan
2) Paging trends and top sources (10m) — Taro/metrics
3) Incident highlights and action updates (15m) — Priya & Samir
4) Runbook updates needed (10m) — Jordan/Maya
5) Decisions: paging priority changes + oncall pilot (10m)
6) AOB / quick blockers (5m)

Action items (tracked)
- Priya: Memory-watermark alert + automated eviction trigger -> JIRA INFRA-4560 (due 2026-03-22)
- Jordan: Update OOM runbook + include checklist for restarts and post-restart verification (due 2026-03-18)
- Samir: PR for fallback warm-up + rollout plan (linked to INFRA-4521) (due 2026-03-29)
- Maya: Add additional router instrumentation for tail latency correlation (due 2026-03-20)
- Taro: Prepare oncall blameless-notes template and page-by-page timeline for SRE-INC-2134 review (due 2026-03-16)

Notes to raise in meeting / questions:
- Prod traffic mix changed — is there an internal customer rollout that explains a rise in batch-heavy requests on 3/10? (Ask product / platform)
- Are we comfortable with the current error budget burn projection? If not, what customer-visibility throttles should we enable?
- Should we temporarily adjust routing policy for us-west-2 during peak until fallback warm-up fix is in place? (cost vs reliability tradeoff)

Misc / scratchpad (for follow-up)
- Check Optimize recommendations for batching thresholds and compare against observed batch sizes on 3/10 (PR: optimize/batching-2026).
- Follow up with infra on whether eviction made it into the hotfix release notes (need to communicate to CS if customer-facing).
- Schedule a short runbook walkthrough next Tue with new SRE hires (walkthrough + tabletop exercise)

References / links:
- Jira SRE incident: SRE-INC-2134 (postmortem draft)
- Jira INFRA-4521 (router fallback PR)
- Confluence runbook: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=987654321

Draft status: initial notes for meeting prep. Will convert to formal meeting minutes after sync and populate action items in JIRA.

---
Jordan (notes to self): remember to export metrics snapshot and attach to meeting invite, add Zoom link, and pin postmortem draft to agenda.
